You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 2 children:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.
  - Blake is 14 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

Regarding Blake:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 14 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by understanding your situation.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age (or if you have multiple children, we can go through them one at a time).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I actually have two children I'd like to ask about - Alex who is 8 years old, and Blake who is 14. Should we go through them one at a time, or can we do both together?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're very welcome - I'm happy to help you with this!

Since both Alex (8 years old) and Blake (14 years old) are **under 16**, they fall into the same age category, which makes this easier. We can assess them together for most questions, as the eligibility rules will be very similar for both of them.

Let me continue with the assessment. For children under 16, the next important question is:

**Are either Alex or Blake working full-time (meaning 24 hours or more per week)?**

This is relevant because even children under 16 won't qualify for Child Benefit if they're working full-time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them work at all. Alex is only 8, so obviously too young for that, and Blake doesn't have any job either - just focuses on school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, that's very clear - thank you! Since neither Alex nor Blake are working full-time, we can move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now the next question:

**Are Alex and Blake NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if either of them receive benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits in their own name

Given their ages (8 and 14), this is quite unlikely, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them receives any benefits in their own name. They're just regular kids - no benefits at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, thank you for confirming that. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! The next question is about apprenticeships:

**Are either Alex or Blake in an apprenticeship?**

Given their ages (8 and 14), they're almost certainly not in apprenticeships, but I need to confirm. Note that certain types of apprenticeships can affect Child Benefit eligibility, though this varies by region (England, Scotland, or Wales).

Can you confirm that neither of them is in any apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. They're both way too young for apprenticeships - Alex is only 8 and Blake is 14. Neither of them is in any apprenticeship program at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected given their ages. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common route)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and your family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with the right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do any of these apply to you?** Most commonly, people simply normally live in the UK - is that your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex and Blake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you meet the residency requirement by normally living in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex and Blake.

**Are you responsible for Alex and Blake?**

You qualify if **ANY** of these apply:

1. **You live with them** (which you've already mentioned you do - you all live together in Manchester)
2. You contribute to their upkeep (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned you live in Manchester with Alex and Blake, it sounds like you live with them - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Both Alex and Blake live at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about other claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex or Blake?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child at a time. For example:
- Is their other parent claiming Child Benefit for them?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other relative) claiming for them?

Or are you the only person claiming (or intending to claim) for both Alex and Blake?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them. I'm the only one who would be claiming for both Alex and Blake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check about Alex and Blake's living situation.

**Are either Alex or Blake currently:**
- In hospital?
- In care (local authority care)?
- Being fostered?
- Or are they both living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me so far, it sounds like they're both living normally at home with you in Manchester, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they're both living normally at home with me. Neither of them is in hospital, in care, or being fostered - just regular home life with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex or Blake's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for their accommodation and maintenance yourself (without the local council contributing)? 

Given that they live at home with you in a normal family situation, I expect the answer is that the council is NOT paying, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance. I pay for everything myself - they just live at home with me as a normal family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Excellent News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE for both Alex and Blake**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for both of your children. Here's why:

✅ **For Alex (age 8):**
- Under 16 years old
- Not working full-time
- Not receiving benefits in their own right
- Living at home with you in a normal family situation

✅ **For Blake (age 14):**
- Under 16 years old
- Not working full-time
- Not receiving benefits in their own right
- Living at home with you in a normal family situation

✅ **Your eligibility as the claimant:**
- You meet UK residency requirements (living in Manchester)
- You're responsible for both children (living with them)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for them
- The local council isn't paying for their accommodation or maintenance

---

## 📝 Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and both children
3. **Provide birth certificates** (or adoption certificates if applicable) for Alex and Blake

---

## 💷 Important Financial Information:

**High Income Child Benefit Charge:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the tax system. However, you can still claim it, and many people choose to do so because claiming protects your National Insurance credits (which count towards your State Pension).

**Payment schedule:** Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits).

---

## 🔗 More Information:

You can find full details about how to claim here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

**Congratulations, and I hope this helps you and your family!** If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
